sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Central Sudanic. In Rainer Vossen & Gerrit J. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, 408-418. Oxford: OUP.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: This work describes Central Sudanic family overview (subgroups MMD, LND, MAS, MEF, SBB); Aja is mentioned only as an 'indeterminate outsider' and as a row in a WALS word-order table, with no description of its phonology. Nothing on Aja stress, accent or tone. The only prosodic statement in the chapter is family-level: 'Typological features include short word shapes (V, CV, VCV, and CVCV), frequent +/-ATR vowel feature (in the south-eastern part of the area), widespread glottalized consonants (see section 4), and tone systems that may include up to four constrastive levels.' (p. 2, section 1).…
sources.venue: The Oxford Handbook of African Languages

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 1250 'aja' (GM = Green & Moran), source Santandrea 1976.https://phoible.org/inventories/view/1250
sources.note: 48 segments (consonants, vowels; tone segments not listed on the page text retrieved); nothing on stress. Cites Santandrea 1976 as the only source.

sources.citation: Santandrea, S. 1948. Little known tribes of the Bahr el Ghazal basin. Sudan Notes and Records 29 (article opens p. 79; Aja paragraph p. 98)
sources.note: Nothing on Aja phonology. p. 98: 'My notes on Aja, show, out of about 230 words, 12 in common with, and 5 similar to, Kresh, as compared with 11 in common with, and 5 similar to, Banda. From a grammatical point of view, Aja seems to stand closer to Kresh, showing Bongo-like elements'. The only accent remark in the article concerns Bviri/Viri (Ndogo group), not Aja.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. 1935. Survey of the language groups in the Southern Sudan. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 7(4): 861-896
sources.note: Aja named once (728 taxpayers) among Western District tribes showing 'remarkable vocabulary resemblance to Bongo and Baka, though no grammatical material is as yet forthcoming'. Nothing on stress or tone.
sources.venue: Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. n.d. Aja Swadesh List (source of the forms not stated). archive.org item rosettaproject_aja_swadesh-1
sources.note: Wordlist only (~200 items, e.g. 'arm: rúʔbú', 'bird: wèri', 'woman: ɔ̀ŋɔ'); some items carry tone diacritics, none carry a stress mark; no prose.

Consonant and vowel tables copied from PHOIBLE/Santandrea 1976; no statement on tone or stress. Kresh languages page: 'Aja.. remains Kresh grammatically, it has been relexified by the unrelated Banda languages (Santandrea 1976)'.
